headline: Revenue rises but earnings sink as margins compress
summary_short: CNH Industrial's Q2 2026 revenue rose 2.0% y/y to $4,803M, but net income attributable to CNH fell 35.2% to $138M and diluted EPS dropped to $0.11 from $0.17 as Agriculture and Construction margins compressed.
summary_long: Consolidated revenue grew 2% y/y to $4.80 billion (net sales of Industrial Activities +3%), but net income fell 35% y/y to $141 million ($138 million attributable to CNH) as diluted EPS dropped to $0.11 from $0.17. Adjusted EBIT margin of Industrial Activities fell 160bps to 4.0%, driven by lower South American agriculture volumes, unfavorable North America/EMEA mix, tariff costs, and higher SG&A/R&D spend; Construction Adjusted EBIT fell to $15 million on tariffs and R&D. Cash fell to $1.87 billion from $2.58 billion at 2025 year-end, largely on debt paydown and YTD share buybacks ($62 million) and dividends. CNH narrowed full-year 2026 guidance to the higher end of prior ranges, including Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.41-$0.46.

drivers.explanation: Net sales of Industrial Activities grew on favorable Agriculture price realization and 12% higher Construction volumes (including shipments delayed from Q1), partly offset by lower South American Agriculture volumes.
Not broken out directly, but segment commentary cites tariff impacts, higher SG&A from labor costs, and higher R&D spend as cost pressures across Agriculture and Construction.
Agriculture Adjusted EBIT fell on lower South America volumes, unfavorable NA/EMEA mix, tariffs, higher SG&A/R&D, and lower JV results; Construction Adjusted EBIT fell on tariffs and higher R&D.
Mirrors the segment-level Adjusted EBIT declines in Agriculture and Construction, plus an 18% drop in Financial Services net income from margin compression and higher Brazil risk costs.

Tracks the net income decline; diluted shares fell modestly (1,241M vs 1,253M) on buybacks, only partly cushioning the per-share drop.
Cash fell as a $835 million net debt paydown and $127 million of dividends paid exceeded $180 million of YTD operating cash flow, per the cash flow statement.
Equity was little changed as YTD net income was largely offset by dividends and buybacks; the release does not itemize the remaining components of the roughly flat move.
Diluted share count declined slightly as $62 million of YTD share repurchases reduced shares outstanding.

CEO Gerrit Marx cited 'disciplined execution... at the trough of the agriculture cycle,' pointing to revenue growth despite pressured farmer economics, while noting improving equipment-cycle indicators like dealer inventory normalization.
